# anchor-x402-safe-pay

> Screen a payment recipient before an AI agent sends funds. A tiny, wallet-agnostic guard that runs an [anchor-x402](https://anchor-x402.com) risk pre-flight (`allow` / `review` / `block`) on the counterparty at the pre-payment chokepoint and **fails closed**. npm + PyPI, MIT. It wraps the send your agent already makes — no new service to call, no account, no API key. One screen call is `$0.02` USDC on Base, settled via x402 by your own paid-fetch.

Use this when an autonomous agent sends USDC/x402 payments and you want a sanctions + address-reputation check (drainer / phishing / mixer) in the send path, so a payment to a flagged address fails closed instead of draining the wallet.

## Install

- npm: `npm install anchor-x402-safe-pay`
- PyPI: `pip install anchor-x402-safe-pay`

## API — JavaScript / TypeScript

- `screen(recipient, { fetchImpl, endpoint?, timeoutMs? }) -> Promise<verdict>` — raw verdict `{ recommendation: "allow"|"review"|"block", risk_score, signals, sanctioned_lists, ... }`.
- `screenAllows(recipient, { fetchImpl, blockOn?, onError?, ... }) -> Promise<{ ok, verdict }>` — no-throw decision; folds `blockOn`/`onError`. Use this to register on an existing pre-pay hook.
- `guardedSend(recipient, sendThunk, { fetchImpl, blockOn?, onError?, ... }) -> Promise<any>` — runs `sendThunk` only if allowed; otherwise throws `ScreenBlockedError` (carrying the verdict) and the send never runs.
- `ScreenBlockedError` — thrown on a blocked verdict; `.verdict` holds the detail.

## API — Python

- `screen(recipient, *, fetch, endpoint=?, timeout=?) -> dict`
- `screen_allows(recipient, *, fetch, block_on=?, on_error=?) -> (ok, verdict)`
- `guarded_send(recipient, send, *, fetch, block_on=?, on_error=?) -> Any` — raises `ScreenBlocked`.

## Minimal use

```js
import { guardedSend } from "anchor-x402-safe-pay";
await guardedSend(recipient, () => wallet.sendUsdc(recipient, amount), { fetchImpl: paidFetch });
```
```python
from anchor_safe_pay import guarded_send
guarded_send(recipient, lambda: wallet.send_usdc(recipient, amount), fetch=paid_post)
```

## Verdict → action

- `allow` → send runs.
- `review` → held by default (elevated risk; wire your own human-in-the-loop to release).
- `block` → held (sanctioned / drainer / phishing).
- unknown / malformed / screen call failed → routed through `onError`; **blocks by default**.

Defaults: `blockOn: ["block","review"]`, `onError: "block"`. Set `blockOn: ["block"]` to send on `review`; set `onError: "allow"` if anchor downtime should never block your payments (choose deliberately).

## Preferred integration: register on the client's existing pre-pay hook (one line, no rewrite)

Most x402 clients already fire a hook with the recipient (`payTo`) before signing — you only need to return a decision. Use a `paidFetch` OTHER than the client you're guarding so screening never recurses.

- Official `@x402` client (`onBeforePaymentCreation`):
  ```js
  x402Client.onBeforePaymentCreation(async (req) => {
    const { ok, verdict } = await screenAllows(req.payTo, { fetchImpl: paidFetch });
    return ok ? undefined : { abort: true, reason: verdict.recommendation };
  });
  ```
- elizaOS plugin-wallet (`onBeforePayment`, return `false` to block):
  ```js
  const onBeforePayment = async (req) => (await screenAllows(req.payTo, { fetchImpl: paidFetch })).ok;
  ```
- faremeter (`payerChooser`, throw to abort), qntx/r402 (`before_payment_creation`), and the Python client (`on_before_payment_creation`) take the same shape — see `examples/`.

## Notes for integrators

- `fetchImpl` (JS) / `fetch` (Py) is required for real use — it settles the `$0.02` screen. Without it you get a 402.
- Screening degrades to a `partial` verdict rather than erroring if the reputation layer is briefly unavailable; `onError` governs total failures.
- Solana recipients: the sanctions floor applies; address-reputation is EVM-oriented, so a Solana verdict may be `partial`.
